Representatives and STL components¶

This notebook recalculates the STL components and strengths from the seed-13 representatives and compares them with the archived reference. The check uses the same fitting function as the terminal route.

Fit the components and calculate their strengths¶

Classical STL with robust weighting decomposes reflectance as Yₜ = Tₜ + Sₜ + Rₜ: trend, seasonal component and residual. The period is 23 calendar positions, the trend window is 45 and the low-pass window is 25; the local polynomial degree is one. Seasonal windows are 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 21, 25, 31 and 35.

Sample variances on the originally observed dates define seasonal strength F_S = max(0, 1 − Var(R)/Var(S+R)) and trend strength F_T = max(0, 1 − Var(R)/Var(T+R)). Time interpolation supplies the regular sequence needed for fitting. Interpolated positions are excluded from the strength calculations; all 173 observed dates per series are included.

Interpret the component figure¶

The 519 selected spectra form 30 series: three classes and ten bands. The displayed table summarises the window-7 strengths by spectral domain; the figure shows its individual-band components. F_T is annotated in trend panels and F_S in seasonal panels. Gray endpoint bands are visual indications; they do not remove dates from the metrics. Window 7 is one of the nine examined configurations and the reference for component differences.
